title: Sidon Sets: Definition and Erdős–Turán Bound
content: A Sidon set (or B₂ set) is a set S of integers in which all pairwise sums a + b (a, b ∈ S, a ≤ b) are distinct, equivalently all differences a - b (a ≠ b, a, b ∈ S) are distinct. Sidon introduced these in the 1930s in connection with Fourier series. The Erdős–Turán theorem (1941) is the fundamental bound: any Sidon subset of {1,...,N} has at most N^(1/2) + O(N^(1/4)) elements. Problem #1206 asks whether the set {n³ : n ≤ N} (N cubes up to N³) contains a Sidon set of size ≫ N—much larger relative to N than the Erdős–Turán bound would predict for a random subset of [1, N³].
mathContext: A set $S \subset \mathbb{Z}$ is Sidon (or $B_2$) if $a + b = c + d$ with $a, b, c, d \in S$ implies $\{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$. Equivalently: the multiset of differences $\{a - b : a \neq b, a, b \in S\}$ has no repeated elements. Erdős–Turán (1941): $|S \cap [1,N]| \leq N^{1/2} + O(N^{1/4})$ for any Sidon set $S$.

title: Why Cubes? The Factoring Trick for n³ - m³
content: The algebraic factoring n³ - m³ = (n-m)(n² + nm + m²) is central to the problem. For two pairs (n₁,n₂) and (n₃,n₄) with n₁ > n₂, n₃ > n₄, the condition n₁³ + n₂³ = n₃³ + n₄³ (Sidon violation) can be rewritten as n₁³ - n₃³ = n₄³ - n₂³. In a short interval near N where n varies by at most cN^(1/2), the quadratic factor n² + nm + m² ≈ 3N² is nearly constant, so differences n^3 - m^3 ≈ (n-m)·3N² are determined primarily by n-m. This forces distinct pairs to have distinct differences—giving the Sidon property.
mathContext: In $[N - cN^{1/2}, N]$: $n^3 - m^3 = (n-m)(n^2 + nm + m^2)$. For $n, m \in [N - cN^{1/2}, N]$: $n^2 + nm + m^2 \in [3(N-cN^{1/2})^2, 3N^2]$, varying by $O(cN^{3/2})$. If $(n_1-n_2) \neq (n_3-n_4)$, then $n_1^3 - n_2^3 \neq n_3^3 - n_4^3$ for small enough $c$, giving the Sidon property.

title: Recent Breakthroughs: Gabdullin–Konyagin 2024, Garaev–Garayev–Konyagin 2026
content: The problem has seen significant recent progress. Gabdullin and Konyagin (2024) proved that for some constant c > 0, the set {n³ : N - cN^(1/2) ≤ n ≤ N} is a Sidon set. This gives a Sidon subset of {n³ : n ≤ N} of size ≫ N^(1/2). In 2026, Garaev, Garayev, and Konyagin improved the exponent: the 1/2 can be raised to 4/7 - o(1) for infinitely many N. For fourth powers (n⁴ instead of n³), they achieve exponent 3/5 for all N. These results push toward the full ≫ N Sidon set the problem asks for.
mathContext: GaKo24: $\{n^3 : N - cN^{1/2} \leq n \leq N\}$ is Sidon — a set of size $\approx cN^{1/2}$. GGK26: exponent improves to $4/7 - o(1)$, meaning size $\gg N^{4/7}$, for infinitely many $N$; and $3/5$ for all $N$ with 4th powers. The open question: can the exponent reach $1$ (i.e., size $\gg N$)?

title: Fifth Powers and Euler's Conjecture Connection
content: The conjecture that {n⁵ : n ≥ 1} is itself a Sidon set is equivalent to the Diophantine statement that a⁵ + b⁵ = c⁵ + d⁵ has no positive-integer solutions with {a,b} ≠ {c,d}. No nontrivial solution is known, and the statement is open. This should not be confused with Euler's sum of powers conjecture (1769), which asserts that summing fewer than k k-th powers can never yield a k-th power; that conjecture was disproved for k = 5 by Lander and Parkin (1966) with 27⁵ + 84⁵ + 110⁵ + 133⁵ = 144⁵ (four fifth powers), and for k = 4 by Elkies (1988). Those are equations of the form (sum of k-th powers) = (single k-th power), structurally different from the two-against-two balance a⁵ + b⁵ = c⁵ + d⁵ that the Sidon property concerns.
mathContext: If $\{n^5 : n \geq 1\}$ is Sidon, then $n_1^5 + n_2^5 \neq n_3^5 + n_4^5$ for distinct unordered pairs. This means the Diophantine equation $a^5 + b^5 = c^5 + d^5$ has no positive integer solutions with $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$ — open as of 2025. Contrast Euler's sum of powers conjecture $\sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x_i^k = y^k$, disproved for $k=5$ (Lander–Parkin 1966) and $k=4$ (Elkies 1988).
prerequisites: distinction between Sidon balance and Euler-type sums

title: The g_k Function: Extremal Sidon Sets Among k-th Powers
content: Erdős defined g_k(A) as the maximal size of a Sidon set of {a^k : a ∈ A}. The conjecture is that g_k(A) ≥ g_k({1,...,N}) for all sets A with |A| = N—that is, among all N-element sets, the 'canonical' set {1,...,N} produces the smallest k-th power Sidon set. This is an extremal problem: is {n^k : n ≤ N} the hardest set to extract a Sidon set from? Related results (Problem [530] for linear case, Problem [773] for squares) suggest this is part of a broader Erdős program on extremal additive combinatorics.
mathContext: Define $g_k(A) = \max\{|S| : S \subseteq \{a^k : a \in A\}, S \text{ is Sidon}\}$. The conjecture: for all $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ with $|A| = N$, $g_k(A) \geq g_k(\{1,\ldots,N\})$. If true, this would characterize the Sidon density of k-th powers in terms of $g_k(\{1,\ldots,N\})$.

title: Formalization Architecture: Axiomatized Reduction
content: The formalization is complete with 0 sorries but is `axiomatized`: the two hard analytic facts are stated as axioms and the gallery result is derived from them. `sidon_in_cubes` (line 82) takes `gabdullin_konyagin_2024` as a hypothesis (a Sidon set `nearTopCubes N k` of size ≥ c√N exists for N ≥ 2) and packages it into the eventual-in-N form `∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ cubeSet N, IsSidon S ∧ S.card ≥ c√N`; the small-N branch is discharged with the empty set (vacuously Sidon). `erdos_1206` (line 97) is then definitionally `sidon_in_cubes`. The only genuine Lean reasoning here is the bookkeeping reduction — `nearTopCubes N k ⊆ cubeSet N` via `simp` and the cardinality bound via `Finset.card_image_le` — while the combinatorial substance (that the short-interval cube set is Sidon) is imported as the axiom. This honestly separates 'what is proved in Lean' from 'what is assumed from the literature'.
mathContext: `sidon_in_cubes : ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∃ S ⊆ cubeSet N, IsSidon S ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≥ c * Real.sqrt N`, proved from the axiom `gabdullin_konyagin_2024`. Reduction uses `Finset.card_image_le` and `nearTopCubes N k ⊆ cubeSet N`. The set lives in `Finset ℕ`, not `Finset ℤ`.

title: Core Definitions: IsSidon, cubeSet, nearTopCubes
content: Three definitions set up the statement. `IsSidon S` (line 34) encodes the Sidon property over `Finset ℕ` in ordered, sum-based form: for all a,b,c,d ∈ S with a ≤ b and c ≤ d, the equality a + b = c + d forces a = c ∧ b = d. The ordering hypotheses a ≤ b, c ≤ d canonicalize each pair so that distinctness of sums is equivalent to distinctness of unordered pairs — this avoids the ∨ (a=c∧b=d) ∨ (a=d∧b=c) disjunction. `cubeSet N` (line 42) is `(Finset.Icc 1 N).image (· ^ 3)`, the cubes {1³,…,N³}. `nearTopCubes N k` (line 49) is the short-interval set `(Finset.Icc (N-k) N).image (· ^ 3)` whose Sidon property is the content of the Gabdullin–Konyagin theorem. Note Icc starts at 1 for cubeSet (excluding 0³=0), matching the problem's {1,…,N} index range.
mathContext: `IsSidon S := ∀ a b c d ∈ S, a ≤ b → c ≤ d → a + b = c + d → a = c ∧ b = d`. `cubeSet N := (Icc 1 N).image (n ↦ n^3)`; `nearTopCubes N k := (Icc (N-k) N).image (n ↦ n^3)`.

title: The Two Axioms: Erdős–Turán Bound and Gabdullin–Konyagin
content: The file's two assumptions (axiomCount = 2) are both deep results imported rather than reproved. `sidon_upper_bound` (line 61) states the Erdős–Turán upper bound in the convenient form |S| ≤ 2√M + 1 for a Sidon set S ⊆ {1,…,M}; this follows from counting the C(|S|,2) distinct pairwise differences, all lying in [1, M], but the clean Lean proof is nontrivial and is taken as an axiom here. `gabdullin_konyagin_2024` (line 74) is the genuine research input: ∃ c > 0 such that for every N ≥ 2 there is k ≥ c√N with `nearTopCubes N k` Sidon. Its proof rests on the short-interval estimate for n²+nm+m², far beyond what is reconstructed in this file. Stating these as `axiom` declarations (rather than `sorry`) is the honest convention for results whose proofs live in the literature: the badge is `axiom` and status `axiomatized`, not `verified`.
mathContext: Axiom 1: $S \subseteq [1,M]$ Sidon $\Rightarrow |S| \leq 2\sqrt M + 1$ (Erdős–Turán shape). Axiom 2: $\exists c>0,\ \forall N\geq 2,\ \exists k \geq c\sqrt N,\ \mathrm{IsSidon}(\mathrm{nearTopCubes}\,N\,k)$ (Gabdullin–Konyagin 2024).
